usageNotes: This endpoint upgrades the HTTP connection to a WebSocket tunnel for VNC traffic and must always be preceded by a call to the vncproxy endpoint (post_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_vncproxy), which returns the required port (5900–5999) and vncticket. The WebSocket handshake is handled by the Proxmox noVNC proxy; callers should not attempt to open this as a plain HTTP GET — it will only work when the client negotiates a WebSocket upgrade. The vncticket is short-lived, so the WebSocket connection must be initiated immediately after the vncproxy call.

examples.summary: Open VNC WebSocket for VM 101 on node pve1 using port and ticket from a prior vncproxy call

tips: Always call post_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_vncproxy first — the port and vncticket it returns are required inputs here.
The port range is 5900–5999; Proxmox allocates from this pool dynamically per vncproxy call.
The vncticket expires quickly; open the WebSocket connection within a few seconds of receiving it.
API tokens are allowed (allowtoken: true), so service accounts can automate console access without a user session.
The caller needs VM.Console privilege on /vms/{vmid} — ensure the token or user has this role assigned.
